record.title: Kerov's positivity conjecture for character polynomials
record.statement:
For each permutation $\pi$, let $K_{\pi}$ be the universal Kerov character polynomial defined by

$$
\Sigma^{\lambda}_{\pi}=K_{\pi}(R_2^{\lambda},R_3^{\lambda},\dots).
$$

For a cycle of length $k$, write $K_k$ for the corresponding polynomial. **Kerov's conjecture.** The coefficients of $K_k$, for $k\geq 1$, are non-negative integers.

This conjecture predicts a positivity property for the exact character formulas expressed through free cumulants. The source reports that it was formulated from numerical evidence; no resolution is supplied here.
record.source_name: Maciej Dołega, Valentin Féray and Piotr Sniady, “Explicit combinatorial interpretation of Kerov character polynomials as numbers of permutation factorizations”, arXiv:0810.3209 (2011).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2007–2008). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:0710.2454](https://arxiv.org/abs/0710.2454).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0810.3209

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2008).

value.title: The circuit-relation ideal conjecture for 3-connected matroid extensions
value.literal_statement:
Let ${\mathbb{P}}$ be a partial field, let $M$ be a 3-connected ${\mathbb{P}}$-representable matroid, and let $N=M{-} e$ be a 3-connected deletion that settles $M$. Let $I_{N,M}$ be the ideal describing the quotient from the representation ring of $N$ to that of $M$, and let $\operatorname{Cr}(N)$ denote the relevant set of cross-ratios of $N$. **Circuit-relation ideal conjecture.** If $N=M{-} e$, $N$ and $M$ are 3-connected, and $N$ settles $M$, then $I_{N,M}$ is an ideal generated by relations $p-q$, where $p,q\in\operatorname{Cr}(N)$.

This conjecture proposes that the constraints imposed by extending a settled 3-connected matroid are generated by pairwise relations between cross-ratios of the smaller matroid. The source gives no evidence that the claim has been resolved.

value.title: Snevily's conjecture for finite abelian groups of odd order
value.literal_statement: Let $G$ be a multiplicatively written abelian group of odd order, and let $A=\{a_1,\ldots,a_k\}$ and $B=\{b_1,\ldots,b_k\}$ be two $k$-subsets of $G$. **Snevily's conjecture.** There is a permutation $\pi\in S_k$ such that $a_1b_{\pi(1)},\ldots,a_kb_{\pi(k)}$ are distinct. This conjecture concerns distinct representatives in products of two subsets of an abelian group; the paper notes that it is known for cyclic groups of odd order and that its validity follows from the determinant conjecture stated later for general finite abelian groups.

value.title: The alternating-sign recurrence conjecture for spanning trees of graph products
value.literal_statement: Let $G$ be any graph, and write $G_n=G\times P_n$. Let $T_n$ denote the number of spanning trees of $G_n$, which satisfies a linear recurrence by the preceding result. **Alternating-sign recurrence conjecture.** The recurrence for $\{T_n\}$ has coefficients that alternate in sign. This conjecture predicts a sign pattern for the linear recurrences governing spanning-tree counts of graph products with paths; the source provides no evidence of resolution.

record.title: The induced-subposet conjecture for weighted games
record.statement: Let $J_n$ be the poset of linear games on $n$ voters, and let $\mathcal{W}_n$ be the weighted games poset, consisting of all weighted voting systems on $n$ voters with the partial ordering induced by the covering relation in $J_n$. **Weighted-games induced-subposet conjecture.** The weighted games poset $\mathcal{W}_n$ is an induced subposet of $J_n$. This asks whether every saturated chain in $J_n$ between two weighted games can be chosen to consist entirely of weighted games; the paper does not give a resolution.
record.source_name: Sarah Mason and Jason Parsley, “A geometric and combinatorial view of weighted voting”, arXiv:1109.1082 (2016).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1109.1082

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2011).
